traits.stamens.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 362: Simpson's formula: stamens 5 to 8, rarely 4 to 10 or more (description: 4 to many).

traits.corolla_shape.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 362: 4 to 5 free petals, often with a scale at the base. Free petals: rotate by PlantGen's free-petal rule; the book names no other corolla form.

traits.note: Jepson's Manual of the Flowering Plants of California (1925), read in full, as Aceraceae, with family summaries (Hamburg's Botany Online, G. Carr, FloraBase) as search results quote them (the pages themselves were not read): flowers actinomorphic or zygomorphic, 4- or 5-merous, with a nectar disk rather than a floral cup; ovary superior, usually of 3 carpels (2 in the maples).

generator.program.note: The program the authors chose to grow this taxon's species (named in each species' spec until G2.3a moved it here).

traits.woodiness.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 215 Sapindaceae (soapberries, horse chestnuts apart) and 219 Aceraceae (maples), which APG joins as Sapindaceae: trees, shrubs or climbers; leaves alternate, very rarely opposite, in the first, opposite in the maples; stipules rarely present.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 215 Sapindaceae (soapberries, horse chestnuts apart) and 219 Aceraceae (maples), which APG joins as Sapindaceae: trees, shrubs or climbers; leaves alternate, very rarely opposite, in the first, opposite in the maples; stipules rarely present.

traits.stipules.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 215 Sapindaceae (soapberries, horse chestnuts apart) and 219 Aceraceae (maples), which APG joins as Sapindaceae: trees, shrubs or climbers; leaves alternate, very rarely opposite, in the first, opposite in the maples; stipules rarely present.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Sapindaceae with Aceraceae, Hippocastanaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 362-364, family Sapindaceae: leaves usually spiral, but opposite in Hippocastanoideae (Acer, Aesculus), whose pairs cross. Read as {"spiral": "usually", "decussate": "sometimes"}.

traits.leaf_division.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 362, 363, 364, family Sapindaceae: leaf division simple, palmate, trifoliolate, pinnate or bipinnate; read as {"compound": "often", "simple": "often"}.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 362, 363, 364, family Sapindaceae: inflorescence cyme, thyrse or raceme, sometimes umbel- or corymb-like, usually; read as {"cyme": "often", "panicle": "often", "raceme": "often", "corymb": "sometimes", "umbel": "sometimes"}. The books add solitary (rarely): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 362, 363, 364: solitary.

traits.fruit_type.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 362, 363, 364, family Sapindaceae: fruit type fleshy or dry; schizocarp, capsule, nut and others; read as {"capsule": "often", "nut": "often", "schizocarp": "often"}.

traits.hypanthium.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add true (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 362, 363, 364: true.

traits.carpels.note: Rare extremes noted only; the count's source is the family's `traits` note. The books give the family low 2: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 362, 363, 364: 2-3 [-6], fused. Left out of the range on the owner's go (2026-10-15): they belong to some of its genera, and a family's rare ends would reach every species that inherits its count.
